html:
Japan from the Meiji Restoration of 1868 to the postwar constitution of 1947, the years in which it became an industrial power and a colonial empire. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

In the name of the young Meiji Emperor, a group of samurai reformers abolished the domains, ended the samurai class and built a conscript army. The last great samurai revolt, the Satsuma Rebellion, was crushed in 1877. Japan built railways, factories and schools for all, took the Ryukyu Islands in 1879 and adopted the Meiji Constitution in 1889.

By 1900 it had won the First Sino-Japanese War of 1894 and 1895 and taken Taiwan. It went on to beat Russia in the Russo-Japanese War of 1904 and 1905, annex Korea in 1910 and seize Manchuria in 1931. Its war in Asia and the Pacific ended in defeat after the atomic bombings of 1945 and was followed by American occupation. The story goes on in Modern Japan.
